# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_002_page_001.jpg

---

*[The speech of the ungodly begins at 2:1 and extends through 2:20]*

2:1 For they reasoned among themselves, not rightly, saying: "Short and sorrowful is our life, and there is no remedy when a man comes to his end, and no one is known to have returned from Hades.

2:2 Because we were born by mere chance, and hereafter we shall be as though we had never been; because the breath in our nostrils is smoke, and reason is a spark kindled by the beating of our hearts,

2:3 which being extinguished, the body will turn to ashes, and the spirit will dissolve like empty air.

2:4 And our name will be forgotten in time, and no one will remember our works; and our life will pass away like the traces of a cloud, and will be scattered like a mist, pursued by the rays of the sun and overcome by its heat.

2:5 For our time is a passing shadow, and there is no putting back of our end; because it is sealed up, and no one turns back.

2:6 Come, therefore, let us enjoy the good things that are present, and let us make use of creation with eagerness as in youth.

2:7 Let us drink our fill of costly wine and perfumes, and let no spring flower pass us by.

2:8 Let us crown ourselves with rosebuds before they wither.

2:9 Let none of us be without share of our revelry; everywhere let us leave signs of gladness, because this is our portion and this lot is ours.

2:10 Let us oppress the righteous poor man; let us not spare the widow, nor respect the grey hairs of the old man.

2:11 But let our strength be our law of righteousness; for what is weak is convicted of being useless.

2:12 Let us lie in wait for the righteous man, because he is inconvenient to us and opposes our actions, and reproaches us for sins against the law, and accuses us of sins against our training.

2:13 He professes to have knowledge of God, and calls himself a child of the Lord.

2:14 He became to us a reproof of our thoughts; he is grievous to us even to behold,

2:15 because his manner of life is unlike that of others, and his ways are wholly different.

2:16 We are counted by him as something base, and he avoids our ways as uncleannesses; he calls the last end of the righteous happy, and boasts that God is his father.

2:17 Let us see if his words are true, and let us test what will come to pass at the end of his life.

2:18 For if the righteous man is God's son, he will help him, and will deliver him from the hand of his adversaries.

2:19 Let us test him with insult and torture, so that we may find out how gentle he is, and make trial of his forbearance.

2:20 Let us condemn him to a shameful death; for, according to what he says, he will be protected."

2:21 Such were their reasonings; but they were led astray, because their wickedness blinded them,

2:22 and they did not know the mysteries of God, nor did they hope for the wages of holiness, nor did they discern the honor accorded to blameless souls.

2:23 Because God created man for incorruption, and made him an image of his own eternity;

2:24 but through the envy of the devil, death entered into the world, and those who belong to his portion experience it.

---

*EMET notes: The speech of the ungodly (vv. 1–20) is one of the most philosophically dense passages in deuterocanonical literature — echoing Qohelet and anticipating Epicurean carpe diem. Key Greek: phthora (death/destruction), aphtharsia (incorruption, v. 23), eikōn (image, v. 23). Verse 23 introduces a key theological claim: humanity was made for incorruption — a direct refutation of the speech that preceded it.*
